===============================================================================
 Actiontec (Realtek RTD1295) install.img  --  ROOTED build
 Dell S718QL projector  --  authorized owner modification of own device
 Built: 2026-10-11
===============================================================================

PURPOSE
  Produce a flashable install.img that guarantees the owner a persistent,
  network-reachable ROOT shell on the Actiontec/Realtek RTD1295 module.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE TASK PREMISE
  The task assumed this module is Android (adbd / ro.secure / ro.debuggable /
  build.prop). It is NOT. The rootfs is a BusyBox + glibc embedded Linux
  (SysV/BusyBox init, /etc/inittab, /sbin/init->busybox) -- a ScreenBeam-style
  wireless-display appliance. There is no Android property system, no *.prop,
  no init*.rc, and no adbd anywhere in the image. The Android rooting knobs do
  not exist and could not be set. Root access was delivered the Linux way
  (an always-on, unauthenticated root shell service), which is the faithful
  equivalent of "adbd running as root with ro.secure=0".

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTAINER FORMAT (reverse-engineered this build)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  install.img = [ GNU tar archive, padded to a 512-byte block boundary,
                  ending at offset 177213440 ]
              + [ 32 ASCII-hex bytes = md5( bytes[0 : 177213440] ) ]
  This trailing MD5 is the package integrity gate (a known Realtek install.img
  pattern). secure_boot=0 and signature="" in config.txt => no RSA/efuse
  signature check (install_a's do_sha256 / sha256_sig path is gated off).
  config.txt carries NO per-image verify=/checksum= tokens, so editing a
  partition trips no stored per-part hash. install_a itself does not parse the
  tar ("Install_a doesn't parse the tarfile"); an outer step untars, install_a
  burns the extracted files.

  Tar member order (physical, preserved EXACTLY, unchanged):
    ALSADaemon, config.txt, customer.tar, generic/,
    generic/gold.rescue.emmc.uImage, generic/rootfs.ext4.bin,
    generic/etc.ext4.bin, generic/gold.rescue.emmc.dtb, generic/emmc.uImage,
    generic/android.emmc.dtb, generic/bluecore.audio,
    generic/gold.bluecore.audio, generic/factory.tar, generic/bootloader.tar,
    generic/gold.rescue.root.emmc.cpio.gz_pad.img, generic/bootfile.image,
    install_a, mke2fs, teeUtility.tar

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
BUILD METHOD (in-place splice -- strongest round-trip guarantee)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Rather than re-tar (which would perturb GNU metadata), the modified
  rootfs.ext4.bin was spliced byte-for-byte into the original tar at its exact
  data offset (12366848, length 112051200), then the 32-byte MD5 trailer was
  recomputed. Everything outside the rootfs data region and the final 32 bytes
  is therefore literally the original bytes.

  ROUND-TRIP PROOF (golden rule): splicing the UNMODIFIED rootfs back and
  recomputing the trailer reproduced the source BYTE-IDENTICALLY
  (SHA256 == 20de0ab4..., `cmp` clean). Guarantee achieved: BYTE-IDENTICAL for
  unmodified input; for the modified build, differences are provably confined
  to (a) the rootfs.ext4.bin region and (b) the recomputed MD5 trailer -- 0
  differing bytes anywhere else (562 diff ranges: 555 in the ext4 region, 7 in
  the 32-byte trailer, 0 elsewhere). Tar member list/order/sizes IDENTICAL.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXACT CHANGE INSIDE rootfs.ext4.bin  (/ partition, mounted at /)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  rootfs.ext4.bin  BEFORE SHA256 f239f54bb6063704b9122448f1b4c33b5dad4b2592c45453037c75f67dcd219d
                   AFTER  SHA256 d69ddbd12b6e4d0a6c626f5b8bb2eb2b0a39376c1002a06d7271d3d02e49a5b0
                   size unchanged (112051200); e2fsck -fn clean before & after.

  ADDED one file (nothing else modified/removed):
    /etc/init.d/S98adbroot   mode 0755, owner root:root, 1077 bytes
      Starts  `/usr/sbin/telnetd -l /bin/sh -p 1023 &`  from rcS at boot.
      BusyBox telnetd with -l /bin/sh spawns /bin/sh directly (no login, no
      password); started by init it runs as ROOT. This is the adbd-as-root
      analog: an always-on, network-reachable, unauthenticated root shell.
      Reach it with:  telnet <device-ip> 1023
      rcS runs /etc/init.d/S??* in order, so S98adbroot auto-starts after
      networking (S40network) and inetd (S41inetd); persistent across reboot
      because it lives on the flashed rootfs partition.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT-ACCESS LEVERS (what grants root on this image)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Pre-existing in the STOCK image (left intact, documented, not relied upon):
    * /etc/shadow: root has an EMPTY password  (root::...)
    * /etc/inittab: getty on serial ttyS0 @115200 -> passwordless root console
    * /etc/inetd.conf: telnet enabled + S41inetd starts inetd -> telnet :23
      reaches /bin/login which accepts empty-password root
    * /bin/busybox is setuid-root; /bin/su present
  Added by this build (the guaranteed, login-free path):
    * /etc/init.d/S98adbroot -> telnet :1023 == direct root /bin/sh, no auth
  su: NOT added as a separate binary -- busybox `su` already present & setuid;
      a standalone su is unnecessary.
  SELinux: N/A (BusyBox Linux, no SELinux policy); nothing set permissive.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RISK / FLASH-SAFETY FINDINGS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  * secure_boot=0 and signature="" => bootloader/updater does NOT reject a
    modified image on a signature. Verified against install_a strings (the
    do_sha256/signature path is the secure-boot branch, gated off here).
  * Package MD5 trailer recomputed exactly => passes the integrity gate.
  * dm-verity: NOT present. /etc/fstab mounts / as plain ext2/ext4 (ro,noauto);
    this is BusyBox Linux, not AVB/verity Android. Editing the rootfs does NOT
    require disabling verity or recomputing a hash tree. No verity brick risk.
  * GOLD / rescue images ARE in this package (config.txt: GOLDrescueDT,
    GOLDRootFS, GOLDKernel, GOLDaudio; install_rescue_root=y) => a bad flash is
    recoverable. Lowest-risk SoC target to experiment on.
  * Residual security note (by design, matches the requested posture): the
    added service is an UNAUTHENTICATED root shell on TCP 1023, reachable by
    anyone on the device's network. This mirrors "adbd + ro.secure=0". The
    stock image is already similarly open (telnet :23 + empty root password).
  * NOT flashed to hardware (per instructions). Round-trip proven in software
    only.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UNDO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  * To revert to stock: reflash the pristine SOURCE install.img
    (SHA256 20de0ab4...), or a GOLD rescue image.
  * To revert just this change inside a rootfs image: delete
    /etc/init.d/S98adbroot and recompute the MD5 trailer (re-splice). The
    pre-existing levers (empty root password, telnet :23, serial getty) are
    stock and were not altered.
  * Rebuild command:
      python3 -I <scratch>/scripts/build_install_img.py \
        "<SOURCE install.img>" <modified rootfs.ext4.bin> dist/actiontec/install.img
===============================================================================
